data.synopsis: GmbHLHm1 is important to the soybean rhizobium symbiosis because loss of activity results in a reduction of nodule fitness and growth. Transcriptional changes in nodules highlight downstream signaling pathways involving circadian clock regulation, nutrient transport, hormone signaling, and cell wall modification.

Reduced levels of nodulation, reduced acetylene reduction, and limited nodule development. Aborted and deformed infection threads restricted to epidermal root hair cells. The few nodules that did form had very low rhizobial colonization and nitrogenase activity.
